\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{തിരിച്ചെടുക്കുക} (tiricceṭukkuka)}{തിരിച്ചെടുക്കുക (tiricceṭukkuka)}]{\ml{തിരിച്ചെടുക്കുക} (tiricceṭukkuka) — to take back}

\label{lesson:ML-C494-tiriccetukkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to test, then the Malayalam for to swap for another.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{തിരിച്ചെടുക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{തിരിച്ചെടുക്കുക}} — \emph{tiricceṭukkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to take back\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{കേടായ} \ml{സാധനം} \ml{കട} \ml{തിരിച്ചെടുത്തു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kēṭāya sādhanaṁ kaṭa tiricceṭuttu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shop took back the faulty item.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{തിരിച്ചെടുത്തു}, \emph{tiricceṭuttu}.

\ml{തിരിച്ച്}, back, plus \ml{എടുക്കുക}, to take.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{തിരിച്ചെടുക്കുക}} (\emph{tiricceṭukkuka}) is a native Dravidian compound of \ml{തിരിച്ച്}, back (DEDR 3246), and \ml{എടുക്കുക}, to take (DEDR 851).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tiricceṭukkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tiricceṭukkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kēṭāya sādhanaṁ kaṭa tiricceṭuttu.} — The shop took back the faulty item.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to test, then the Malayalam for to swap for another, then say \emph{tiricceṭukkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{തിരിച്ചെടുക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To take back\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ചെലവ്} (celavŭ)}{ചെലവ് (celavŭ)}]{\ml{ചെലവ്} (celavŭ) — an expense; a cost}

\label{lesson:ML-C494-celavu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to swap for another, then the Malayalam for to take back.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ചെലവ്}}
\textbf{\ml{ചെലവ്}} — \emph{celavŭ} — \textquotedblleft{}an expense; a cost\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{യാത്രയുടെ} \ml{ചെലവ്} \ml{ഞങ്ങൾ} \ml{പങ്കുവച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yātrayuṭe celavŭ ñaṅṅaḷ paṅkuvaccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We shared the cost of the trip.
\end{quote}

You met the verb \ml{ചെലവഴിക്കുക}, to spend: literally to let the cost go.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ചെലവ്}} (\emph{celavŭ}) is native Dravidian, from the root \ml{ചെൽ}, to go or pass: money that goes out (DEDR 2781).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{celavŭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{celavŭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yātrayuṭe celavŭ ñaṅṅaḷ paṅkuvaccu.} — We shared the cost of the trip.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to swap for another, then the Malayalam for to take back, then say \emph{celavŭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ചെലവ്} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An expense; a cost\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഒത്തുനോക്കുക} (ottunōkkuka)}{ഒത്തുനോക്കുക (ottunōkkuka)}]{\ml{ഒത്തുനോക്കുക} (ottunōkkuka) — to tally; to check against}

\label{lesson:ML-C494-ottunokkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to take back, then the Malayalam for an expense.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഒത്തുനോക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ഒത്തുനോക്കുക}} — \emph{ottunōkkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to tally; to check against\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ഞാൻ} \ml{ബിൽ} \ml{സാധനങ്ങളുമായി} \ml{ഒത്തുനോക്കി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ñān bil sādhanaṅṅaḷumāyi ottunōkki.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I checked the bill against the goods.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ഒത്തുനോക്കി}, \emph{ottunōkki}.

\ml{ഒത്ത്}, matching, plus \ml{നോക്കുക}, to look. What you compare with takes -\ml{ഉമായി}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഒത്തുനോക്കുക}} (\emph{ottunōkkuka}) is a native Dravidian compound of \ml{ഒത്ത്}, agreeing or matching (DEDR 924), and \ml{നോക്കുക}, to look (DEDR 3794).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ottunōkkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ottunōkkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ñān bil sādhanaṅṅaḷumāyi ottunōkki.} — I checked the bill against the goods.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to take back, then the Malayalam for an expense, then say \emph{ottunōkkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഒത്തുനോക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To tally; to check against\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{എണ്ണിനോക്കുക} (eṇṇinōkkuka)}{എണ്ണിനോക്കുക (eṇṇinōkkuka)}]{\ml{എണ്ണിനോക്കുക} (eṇṇinōkkuka) — to count and check}

\label{lesson:ML-C494-enninokkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for an expense, then the Malayalam for to tally.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{എണ്ണിനോക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{എണ്ണിനോക്കുക}} — \emph{eṇṇinōkkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to count and check\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{കടക്കാരൻ} \ml{തന്ന} \ml{ബാക്കി} \ml{ഞാൻ} \ml{എണ്ണിനോക്കി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kaṭakkāran tanna bākki ñān eṇṇinōkki.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I counted the change the shopkeeper gave me.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{എണ്ണിനോക്കി}, \emph{eṇṇinōkki}.

\ml{എണ്ണി}, having counted, plus \ml{നോക്കുക}: to count to make sure.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{എണ്ണിനോക്കുക}} (\emph{eṇṇinōkkuka}) is a native Dravidian compound of \ml{എണ്ണുക}, to count (DEDR 793), and \ml{നോക്കുക}, to look (DEDR 3794).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eṇṇinōkkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eṇṇinōkkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṭakkāran tanna bākki ñān eṇṇinōkki.} — I counted the change the shopkeeper gave me.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for an expense, then the Malayalam for to tally, then say \emph{eṇṇinōkkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{എണ്ണിനോക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To count and check\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{വിറ്റഴിക്കുക} (viṟṟaḻikkuka)}{വിറ്റഴിക്കുക (viṟṟaḻikkuka)}]{\ml{വിറ്റഴിക്കുക} (viṟṟaḻikkuka) — to sell off}

\label{lesson:ML-C494-virralikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to tally, then the Malayalam for to count and check.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{വിറ്റഴിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{വിറ്റഴിക്കുക}} — \emph{viṟṟaḻikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to sell off\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{കടക്കാരൻ} \ml{പഴയ} \ml{സാധനങ്ങൾ} \ml{വില} \ml{കുറച്ച്} \ml{വിറ്റഴിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kaṭakkāran paḻaya sādhanaṅṅaḷ vila kuṟaccŭ viṟṟaḻiccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shopkeeper sold off the old goods cheaply.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{വിറ്റഴിച്ചു}, \emph{viṟṟaḻiccu}.

\ml{വിറ്റ്}, having sold, plus \ml{അഴിക്കുക}, to let loose: to sell until nothing is left.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{വിറ്റഴിക്കുക}} (\emph{viṟṟaḻikkuka}) is a native Dravidian compound of \ml{വിൽക്കുക}, to sell (DEDR 5421), and \ml{അഴിക്കുക}, to loosen or spend (DEDR 277).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{viṟṟaḻikkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{viṟṟaḻikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṭakkāran paḻaya sādhanaṅṅaḷ vila kuṟaccŭ viṟṟaḻiccu.} — The shopkeeper sold off the old goods cheaply.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to tally, then the Malayalam for to count and check, then say \emph{viṟṟaḻikkuka} again
\end{itemize}
